label: first x/m/3/g/t input early in the original phase, after c/d/k-like tokens
explanation: Original-phase unit: 99% of activation mass falls in the original phase, peaking at t=3-4 and never firing at t=0 or at the delimiter. It fires when the input is one of x (28% of mass), m, 3, g, t (89% combined; s and v weaker). Activation is strongest when this is the first such token in the sequence and the earlier prefix contains c/d/k (first_tok=c has 5x lift; the top examples look like "c c d x" and "c d 1 x"). It is weaker for repeated tokens and later positions (t>=7). It almost never fires in the copy phase (0.8% of mass, mostly recall_idx 1-2). Precision is low: x/m/3/g/t at early positions often leave it silent, so the prefix dependence is only partly captured by the seen() conditions. Dev F1 is about 0.40 and mass recall about 0.67; a looser predicate without the prefix condition reaches 0.83 mass recall at F1 0.27.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=1: x; t=2: x, 3, m, g; t=3: x, m, 3, g) and the first original token (most: c, k, a, d, n, 2; least: x, e, b, 3); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=9 & t=10, L=9 & t=11.
